title: 40-year-old man with alcohol use and agitation
arrival: A 40-year-old man smells strongly of alcohol. He is yelling at and threatening another patient. He states that he would like to see a doctor. However, when asked for more information, he screams and threatens staff.

checkpoints.why: He is awake, shouting, and speaking.

It is not safe to palpate his pulse because of his agitation. For this exercise an unassessable group is treated as “no” so the walkthrough can continue — but being unable to assess a criterion is not the same as the criterion being absent; it is checked once it is safe.
He is not convulsing, but his glucose cannot be safely checked right now for the same reason. This is treated as “no” for the exercise, not as confirmed absence.
He is violent and aggressive, threatening both another patient and staff.

feedbackWhy: He is violent and threatening other patients and staff. His behaviour poses an immediate safety risk.
teachingPoint: Vital signs do not affect this patient's triage decision and should be obtained only once it is safe to do so.
reviewNote: The source case marks Circulation and Disability as “unable to assess” rather than a clean No (unsafe to approach). This prototype forces both to “No” so the yes/no walkthrough can continue, and explains the nuance in the rationale text. Confirm whether a distinct “cannot assess” answer option should be added instead.
